item.title: Morocco rejects Ceuta crossing accusations
item.description: Morocco's foreign ministry said on Thursday that no evidence established involvement of Rabat in the mass crossing into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in July, adding it rejected being drawn into Spain's domestic political battles.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Eljechtimi
item.content:encoded: Morocco's foreign ministry said on Thursday that no evidence established involvement of Rabat in the mass crossing into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in July, adding it rejected being drawn into Spain's domestic political battles. More than 70,000 people crossed from Morocco into Ceuta, fueling [USN:L8N44Z0HP TEXT:"criticism"] in Spain of both Rabat and Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez. While most have since returned, over 100 died according to NGOs. Local authorities say thousands, including unaccompanied minors, remain in the enclave, living in makeshift camps or on the streets and beaches, fuelling near-daily protests by residents angry at the Spanish government's handling of the crisis. Spain's opposition parties have since targeted Pedro Sanchez's government's relationship with Morocco and accused Rabat of facilitating or orchestrating the crossing. "Why continue to level accusations against Morocco when no evidence, facts, or reports establish any involvement on the part of Moroccan authorities?" the ministry said in a statement. "Why are illegal migrants not being returned, even though the Moroccan government has officially committed to readmitting them? Why are unaccompanied minors being kept away from their families, when Morocco has urgently requested their return?" the ministry said. [USN:L8N45121W TEXT:"Reports"] released by the Spanish government on Wednesday showed that Spanish intelligence and security agencies had warned both Madrid and Moroccan counterparts about the possibility of a mass crossing. "Morocco refuses to be used as a pre-election political pawn, nor does it accept being made the scapegoat in political score-settling," the ministry said. National elections are due in Spain by mid-2027. The ministry highlighted the close security, migration and economic cooperation established between Rabat and Madrid since Sanchez backed in 2022 Morocco's autonomy plan for Western Sahara. Morocco does not recognise Spanish sovereignty over Ceuta and the other enclave of Melilla.

item.title: Rafael Márquez asume como DT de selección México con ilusión de conseguir títulos
item.description: Rafael Márquez asumió el jueves como director técnico de la selección mexicana de fútbol con la ilusión de lograr los éxitos que tuvo en su carrera como jugador y aprovechar el aprendizaje que adquirió como asistente técnico de Javier Aguirre en el pasado Mundial.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rafael Márquez asumió el jueves como director técnico de la selección mexicana de fútbol con la ilusión de lograr los éxitos que tuvo en su carrera como jugador y aprovechar el aprendizaje que adquirió como asistente técnico de Javier Aguirre en el pasado Mundial. Márquez, quien disputó con la selección de México cinco Mundiales, fue confirmado como técnico de la selección en julio, oficializando el relevo previsto desde 2024 tras la salida de Javier Aguirre al término de la Copa del Mundo. "Ojalá que algún día podamos tener el éxito que obtuve como jugador, la ventaja es que no empezamos de cero, hay que mantener lo que tenemos, pero hay que mejorar y evolucionar, hay un margen de mejora importantísimo. Lo que hay de base me da esa confianza de que el equipo va a competir, a luchar y a dar lo mejor en cada partido, y esperamos que los resultados acompañen, queremos potencializar al fútbol mexicano con gente de nivel y calidad", dijo Márquez tras su presentación como técnico de la selección. "Hoy tengo esta oportunidad, sabemos que va a haber momentos complicados, pero con la confianza de que vamos a salir adelante. Busco hacer algo diferente en el Mundial y ojalá que se pueda dar, estoy muy contento de representar a México ahora en esta posición y ojalá que las cosas vayan bien", agregó. En su etapa como jugador, Márquez militó en el Barcelona del 2003 al 2010, período en el que conquistó cuatro ediciones de la liga española, tres Supercopas de España y una Copa del Rey. Además, dos ediciones de la Liga de Campeones, una Supercopa de Europa y un Mundial de Clubes. También jugó para el Mónaco de Francia y con el New York Red Bulls de la MLS de Estados Unidos. En México militó en el León y Atlas, donde inició su carrera en 1996. Con la selección de México acumuló 148 partidos internacionales y conquistó la Copa Confederaciones de 1999. El ahora técnico del "Tri" -como llaman los mexicanos a su selección- agradeció el aprendizaje que tuvo como asistente técnico de Javier Aguirre durante el proceso que inició en 2024 y que culminó en la pasada Copa del Mundo, donde México fue eliminado por Inglaterra en los octavos de final. Antes de integrarse al cuerpo técnico de Aguirre, Márquez inició su carrera como entrenador en las categorías formativas del RSD Alcalá de España y posteriormente dirigió al Barcelona Atlètic. "Muy contento, feliz e ilusionado de tomar esta responsabilidad. Estoy muy agradecido con Javier (Aguirre) de abrirme las puertas de su cuerpo técnico y aprender, el resultado obtenido en la Copa del Mundo me deja un buen sabor de boca, hay una continuidad y una base importante, y me tiene muy ilusionado el hacer crecer esta selección", señaló el ex jugador de 47 años. "No es que vaya a partir de cero, me da mucha confianza seguir con este proceso, con algo que ya conozco bastante, me he cobijado de un grupo de gente con experiencia, lo que queremos es tratar de llevar a esta selección a otro nivel. Me deja muy tranquilo lo que se hizo en estos dos años, la confianza que me dio Javier Aguirre y la experiencia que me dejó, ha sido un gran aprendizaje estar con Javier", apuntó. El debut de Márquez como seleccionador será el 26 de septiembre en un partido amistoso ante Colombia, y tres días después enfrentarán a Perú. Posteriormente, en octubre, México jugará ante Estados Unidos y Chile. "Nos estamos enfocando en hacer una lista competitiva, nos vamos a enfrentar a cuatro rivales grandes. Cada uno de los jugadores va a tener que hacer su mejor esfuerzo en sus clubes para poder se considerados, aquí vamos a sacar lo mejor de cada uno de ellos para estar en un mejor nivel", señaló. "Hay un radar de 60 jugadores, más una buena camada de jóvenes que viene empujando fuerte, y vamos a estar muy pendientes de todos ellos. Lo principal y lo que hemos vivido en este último Mundial, es que la gente se sienta orgullosa de su selección, que sean bien representados, que intentemos siempre competir", puntualizó.

item.title: Petrobras eyes diesel price hike, awaiting government measures to shield consumers, sources say
item.description: Brazil's Petrobras is looking to raise diesel prices at its refineries by about 1 real ($0.1964) per liter, but is waiting for government measures to shield consumers from the increase, two sources at the state-run oil firm told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Viga Gaier
item.content:encoded: Brazil's Petrobras is looking to raise diesel prices at its refineries by about 1 real ($0.1964) per liter, but is waiting for government measures to shield consumers from the increase, two sources at the state-run oil firm told Reuters. The hike would help Petrobras narrow the gap between domestic diesel prices and international benchmarks, which has widened due to the conflict in the Middle East and [USN:S8N40Z04X TEXT:"diesel export restrictions"] from Russia. Despite being a diesel producer, Brazil still imports roughly a quarter of its diesel demand. When Petrobras is forced to import fuel at higher international prices than it charges domestically, the margin squeeze hurts profitability. With a 1 real increase, the price gap would almost disappear, one source said. The increase would be possible thanks to a [USN:L1N4510M1 TEXT:"new diesel subsidy"] initially set at 1 real per liter, to be added to an existing one of about 1.12 reais per liter. Details of the measure have yet to be unveiled, however. Petrobras did not immediately reply to a request for comment over the price hike.

item.title: US pipeline operator Kinetik exploring potential sale, sources say
item.description: U.S. pipeline operator Kinetik Holdings is in the early stages of exploring a potential sale of the company, three sources familiar with the matter said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. pipeline operator Kinetik Holdings (KNTK.N) is in the early stages of exploring a potential sale of the company, three sources familiar with the matter said on Wednesday. The move comes at a time of significant interest, both from energy companies and financial investors, in owning energy infrastructure. This is supported by a number of factors, including the importance of supplying natural gas for power generation used by data centers. Headquartered in both Houston and Midland, Texas, Kinetik is working with advisers on the process, said the sources, who cautioned that no deal was guaranteed and spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential deliberations. Investment firm Blackstone (BX.N) controls around 48% of Kinetik, with infrastructure investor I Squared Capital owning roughly 19%, according to regulatory filings. Their ownership traces back to EagleClaw Midstream, which was combined with Altus Midstream in 2022 to create Kinetik. Kinetik and Blackstone declined comment. I Squared did not respond to a comment request. Kinetik focuses on transporting natural gas and crude oil from wells in the Delaware portion of the Permian basin of Texas and New Mexico. It has more than 4,600 miles (7,400 km) of pipelines, as well as associated compression and processing infrastructure, according to its website. Its position in the Permian would make Kinetik an attractive takeover target for another midstream company seeking to grow its operations in the heart of the U.S. shale industry. Dealmaking involving pipeline companies has been robust in recent months. Enbridge (ENB.TO) said on Wednesday it was buying the oil business of privately owned [USN:L4N4511QS TEXT:"Tallgrass Energy"] for $2.55 billion. ONEOK (OKE.N) announced on August 30 it would acquire for $4.43 billion the Midland basin assets of [USN:L6N44R087 TEXT:"Brazos Midstream"] from buyout firms Old Ironsides Energy and EnCap Flatrock Midstream. Bloomberg News had earlier on Wednesday reported Kinetik was exploring sale options, citing people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Precios minoristas de Argentina +1,7% en agosto: INDEC
item.description: El Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) de Argentina registró una variación de 1,7% en el octavo mes del año, luego del 2,1% anotado en julio, informó el jueves el Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC), cifra que estuvo en línea con las estimaciones del mercado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) de Argentina registró una variación de 1,7% en el octavo mes del año, luego del 2,1% anotado en julio, informó el jueves el Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC), cifra que estuvo en línea con las estimaciones del mercado. Un reciente sondeo de [USN:L1N4510HU TEXT:"Reuters"] proyectó que el dato de inflación de agosto se ubicaría en el 1,7%. En el acumulado en lo que va del año, el IPC anotó una variación de 21,3%, mientras que en la medición interanual fue de 33,5%. - Para más información ver

item.title: Trump's $5,000 dividend plan draws some Republican skepticism
item.description: President Donald Trump's promise to send U.S. adults $5,000 dividend checks if his party keeps control of Congress in November's midterm elections drew a cool reception from some Republicans on Thursday, with several lawmakers saying it would spike inflation and worsen the country's fiscal stability.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bogage
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump's promise to send U.S. adults [USN:L1N45203G TEXT:"$5,000 "dividend" checks"] if his party keeps control of Congress in November's midterm elections drew a cool reception from some Republicans on Thursday, with several lawmakers saying it would spike inflation and worsen the country's fiscal stability. Trump told voters at the Republicans' midterm convention in Dallas on Wednesday that he would issue the stimulus checks to celebrate "our tremendous strength and success economically." [USN:L6N45211D TEXT:"The proposal"], if approved by Congress, would [USN:L6N45211D TEXT:"cost roughly $1.2 trillion"], plus hundreds of billions of dollars more in interest. Some Republicans warned the massive cash injection into an economy already running hot could accelerate inflation at a time when voters are concerned about high living costs. "I would personally throw everything of my heart and soul to stop it, because it would actually do more damage to working people than would ever help them," U.S. Representative David Schweikert, an Arizona Republican set to leave Congress at the end of his term, told Reuters on Wednesday. "It would continue to raise interest rates," he added. "It would be on their own credit card and would bring the interest rate death spiral sooner to the United States." SOME REPUBLICANS SUPPORT PLAN Several Republicans quickly backed the proposal, however, as they look for ways to energize voters in the campaign's final stretch. U.S. Senator Bernie Moreno, an Ohio Republican, wrote on social media that he was preparing legislation to formalize the "Trump dividend" after the November 3 election. The debate is unfolding against the backdrop of [USN:L6N44O018 TEXT:"a fiscal reckoning decades in the making"]. Economists across the political spectrum warn that Washington's heavy borrowing — pushing the national debt toward levels unseen since World War Two — has put the country on an unsustainable financial trajectory. Trump has promised other "dividends" before, including payments from tariff revenue and his cost-cutting U.S. Department of Government Efficiency. None have come to fruition. He issued payments to military service members in December 2025, calling them a "warrior dividend." But the $1,776 payments were repurposed funds from military housing stipends and not a Christmas bonus as Trump had described them. "You never know with Trump whether this was just kind of a rhetorical thing, or whether he really meant it," said Stephen Moore, a conservative economist who periodically advises Trump and White House officials. White House spokesman Davis Ingle said in a statement that "the doomers and naysayers have consistently doubted President Trump" and Trump has proven them wrong. "With the continued support of the American people, President Trump will keep delivering real results," Ingle said. Democrats poked fun at Trump's proposal. U.S. Representative Ted Lieu of California wrote on social media : "If Democrats flip the House and Senate everyone will get a $10,000 dividend, and a pony, and free ice cream for life." VOTERS' REACTIONS MIXED At the Republican convention in Dallas, voters' reactions to the proposal were mixed. Christine Gardner, a retired intellectual property lawyer from Texas, said she did a double take when she heard Trump announce the dividend. "I thought that was very strange," Gardner said. "I thought: 'He's buying votes.'" Chris Lorenz, an Oklahoma minister, said he backed the payments, adding that he felt Americans are overtaxed and that Republicans must win in November to prevent Democrats from instituting far-left policies. "I think it's great, $5,000, especially if it'll help win the midterms," he said. "We believe the future of the country is at stake." TRUMP MAKES MIDTERMS A TEST OF HIS PRESIDENCY Trump told voters on Wednesday to cast the midterms as a referendum on his presidency, instructing them to "pretend that I'm on the ballot." But voters have soured on Trump's agenda, recent Reuters/Ipsos polls show. [USN:L6N44S0Y9 TEXT:"Trump's approval rating stands at 33%"]. Most Americans [USN:L6N44S13O TEXT:"oppose his new tariffs on Canadian goods,"] and voters favor Democrats' approach to cost-of-living issues over Republicans' [USN:L6N44M0S0 TEXT:"by an eight-percentage-point margin"]. Senate Majority Leader John Thune, a South Dakota Republican who has sometimes publicly disagreed with Trump, said it was unclear whether the checks could garner the 60 votes needed to defeat a Senate filibuster but that he thought Republicans could keep control of both chambers as they consider additional tax cuts. "We'll cross that bridge when we come to it," he told Fox News. "He wants more money in the pockets of the American people. The Democrats want to grow government in Washington, D.C.," Thune said. "Obviously, we're going to be looking at every opportunity we can to allow the American people to keep more of what they earn."

item.title: Several killed in bus crash near Swiss Alpine village
item.description: A number of people were killed and several others injured after a bus carrying a Dutch tour party flipped over in a remote Alpine region of eastern Switzerland, police said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A number of people were killed and several others injured after a bus carrying a Dutch tour party flipped over in a remote Alpine region of eastern Switzerland, police said on Thursday. Police in the canton of Graubuenden said the accident occurred near to the village of Susch, and images of the scene published online showed the vehicle lying on its side next to the road, surrounded by police and emergency service personnel. A spokeswoman for the General Dutch Association of Travel Companies (ANVR), acting as spokesperson for tour operator OAD, said a serious accident had taken place involving an OAD bus and that 48 passengers were on board, all Dutch nationals. Local authorities did not respond to requests for more details on the number of casualties. Police said they would provide an update in the coming hours.

item.title: Braves bats awaken late to avoid sweep vs. Rays
item.description: Ha-Seong Kim's two-run single was the difference as the Atlanta Braves plated three runs in the eighth inning to break a scoreless tie and roll to a 3-1 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays on Thursday afternoon to salvage the finale of the three-game series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ha-Seong Kim's two-run single was the difference as the Atlanta Braves plated three runs in the eighth inning to break a scoreless tie and roll to a 3-1 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays on Thursday afternoon to salvage the finale of the three-game series. The rally came against Tampa Bay reliever Kevin Kelly (6-4) as the Braves scraped together five straight one-out hits after being held to two total hits through seven innings. Pinch hitter Ozzie Albies rapped a one-out triple off the wall in right field and scored on Austin Riley's sharp single. Mike Yastrzemski followed with a ground-rule double to right and Kim, who entered the game hitting .110, drove a two-run single into center field. Didier Fuentes (6-2) worked a scoreless eighth inning to record the victory. Raisel Iglesias worked around one run in the ninth, a pinch-hit homer by Victor Mesa Jr., to earn his 32nd save. Atlanta (86-61) avoided its first home series sweep of the season and ended its three-game losing streak against Tampa Bay (87-59), which entered having won four of its last five games. The game quickly developed into a pitcher's duel between veterans Nick Martinez of Tampa Bay and Martin Perez of Atlanta. Neither permitted the opposition to score during their time on the mound. The Rays loaded the bases in the first inning against Perez but had the rally squelched when the Braves were able to double up speedy Chandler Simpson on a sharp grounder. Tampa Bay didn't get another hit until Jonny Deluca's two-out single in the sixth. Atlanta had just as much trouble reaching base against Martinez. Kim had an infield single with one out in the sixth -- the Braves' first hit since Matt Olson's first-inning single -- but was picked off. Perez pitched seven innings and allowed four hits and two walks, striking out four. Perez came up short once again in his fifth attempt to earn his 100th career victory. Martinez worked 6 1/3 innings and gave up two hits, striking out three. He has pitched 20 1/3 consecutive scoreless innings over his last three starts against Atlanta. Braves outfielder Lane Thomas was a late scratch with left side tightness. --Field Level Media

item.title: US slaps new sanctions on networks aiding Iran's proxies in Middle East
item.description: The U.S. government announced new sanctions on Thursday against firms and individuals that it says are aiding Hezbollah and other Iranian proxies in the Middle East as it intensified its campaign to isolate Iran economically.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: The U.S. government announced new sanctions on Thursday against firms and individuals that it says are aiding Hezbollah and other Iranian proxies in the Middle East as it intensified its campaign to isolate Iran economically. The latest sanctions are part of the Treasury Department's "Operation Economic Outcast," announced August 24, which aims to cut off Tehran's funding for the war, missile construction, cyberattacks and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, or IRGC. Thursday's actions by Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control hit entities and individuals in Iraq, the United Arab Emirates, Lebanon and Turkey that Washington said supported Kata’ib Hezbollah, an Iraqi Shia paramilitary group under the command of the IRGC, and Hezbollah, a Lebanese Shia party, Treasury said in a statement. Treasury also announced a settlement with a U.S. citizen who agreed to pay $1.43 million to settle their potential civil liability for 39 apparent violations of sanctions on Iran, and issued a broad whistleblower appeal for tips on any sanctions evasion or money laundering by Iran. OFAC issued a bulletin making clear that it would deny most Iran-related licensing requests, except in exceptional circumstances, and said its licensing division had immediately begun denying "the vast majority" of outstanding Iran-related specific license requests. "OFAC will maintain this licensing policy until Iran changes its behavior, including obstructing the Strait of Hormuz, attacking U.S. personnel and partners in the Gulf, and pursuing nuclear and conventional weapons," Treasury said. “Operation Economic Outcast is targeting those who continue to stand with the failing Iranian regime,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement. “Whether they finance terror, launder money, or help Iran evade sanctions, we will find them, cut them off from the U.S. financial system, and dismantle the networks keeping the regime afloat.” The Iran war, now in its seventh month, has dragged down President Donald Trump's approval rating as Americans grapple with far higher gasoline prices, and could threaten his Republican Party's chances of keeping control of Congress in midterm elections in November. Far from the quick U.S. military operation in Venezuela that ousted leader Nicolas Maduro, the Iran war has dragged into a battle of attrition punctuated by attacks on oil tankers that is also spreading to neighboring countries. The new sanctions did not target [USN:L6N45203X TEXT:"Iran-aligned Houthis"], who seized control of Yemen's port city of Mocha on Thursday and advanced down the Red Sea coast, gaining further leverage over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the southern outlet of the Red Sea and one of the world's most important shipping routes. IMPACT ON OIL SHIPMENTS But a U.S. official said Treasury's campaign was hitting Iran's economy hard while the U.S. naval blockade was squeezing Tehran's ability to move oil. Loadings of Iranian oil were down to about 0.2 million barrels per day over the past 30 days from 1.8 million barrels per day in January and February, they said. Offloadings had dropped to 0.9 million barrels per day from 1.4 million barrels per day before the war, the official said. The amount of Iranian or suspected Iranian oil on the water had averaged just 110 million barrels over the past week, down from over 180 million barrels in January and February. Food prices increased sharply, the official said, while the Iranian rial depreciated by about 30% versus the U.S. dollar since the start of the war, the official added. Brett Erickson, managing principal with Obsidian Risk Advisors, said the latest sanctions would have only a marginal impact on Iran’s ability to move hard currency. "These in no way move the needle," he said. "Beyond this, they target Hezbollah, but not the far more consequential Iranian proxy in the Houthis that are wreaking havoc on the global energy markets."

item.title: ウクライナ和平3者協議、ロシア議会選前は開催されず＝ゼレンスキー氏
item.description: [キーウ １０日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[キーウ　１０日　ロイター] - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は１０日、ロシアとの和平実現に向け米国が仲介する協議について、ロシアの議会選挙前にウクライナ、ロシア、米国による３者協議は実施されないとの見方を示した。

ゼレンスキー氏は、ウクライナは米国と緊密に連絡を取っているとし、エネルギー問題や穀物輸出を巡る協議について月内の進展に期待を示した。

ロシアでは９月２０日に議会選挙が実施される。

item.title: ＵＡＥ、独に460億ドルの追加投資へ 関係強化で企業間契約も締結
item.description: [ベルリン １０日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ベルリン　１０日　ロイター] - ドイツとアラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）の首脳は１０日、両国企業間で総額９４億ユーロ相当の契約が締結されたと発表した。また、ＵＡＥがドイツの産業振興を目的とした投資パッケージを打ち出すことも明らかにした。

共同声明によると、ＵＡＥのムハンマド・ビン・ザイド・ナハヤン大統領はドイツを３日間の日程で国賓訪問し、メルツ独首相と会談。「両国および広範な国際秩序にとって重要な節目に行われた」と記した。また両国は、二国間貿易・投資関係を深化させる方針を再確認したと述べた。

投資パッケージは、ドイツの産業競争力と経済成長の強化を目的としており、容量約１ギガワットの新規データセンター開発を含むデジタルインフラへの投資が含まれる。

また、ＵＡＥのスルターン・アル・ジャーベル産業・先端技術相は、ドイツの産業と雇用の支援に向け、４００億ユーロ（４６０億ドル）を追加投資すると発表。「ドイツは数十年にもわたり、わが国の重要な戦略的・経済的パートナーであり、今回の４００億ユーロの追加投資は、今後数年間にわたりその関係に投資していくというわれわれの意欲の表れだ」と述べた。

既存の対独投資３４０億ユーロに上乗せする形で行われる今回の追加投資は、ドイツの産業能力と熟練労働者の雇用を支援し、エネルギー安全保障とサプライチェーン（供給網）を強化することを目的としていると説明した。

item.title: Legal profession is ‘detrimental’ to mental health, say 41% of lawyers
item.description: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com.)
item.dc:creator: Karen Sloan, Mike Scarcella, David Thomas
item.content:encoded: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com .) Lawyers in the United States suffer from elevated anxiety, stress, depression, burnout and problem drinking despite efforts over the past decade to improve attorney wellness and mental health, a new national survey has found. Nearly 22% of lawyers report moderate to severe symptoms of depression, according to the new study the American Bar Association’s Commission on Lawyer Assistance Programs and lawyer mental health advisory firm Krill Strategies published this week in the Journal of Affective Disorders. Drawn from responses of more than 37,000 lawyers, it's the largest study to date on lawyer wellness, according to the authors. Bar associations, law firms and other legal employers have stepped up efforts to address lawyer mental health since an earlier version of the study raised alarms in 2016, said study co-author Patrick Krill, but the new data shows that those initiatives have not done enough. "It shows that the issues were worse than we thought," Krill told Reuters. "The levels of distress were higher than we knew." More than 20% of the surveyed lawyers reported moderate to severe levels of anxiety, while nearly 19% reported those levels for stress. More than 41% reported that time in the legal profession has been “detrimental” to their mental health. The study also found high rates of problem drinking among lawyers, with nearly 42% screening positive for hazardous drinking and 26% of those reporting an even higher level of drinking, on an international tool used to assess alcohol use. Prior research has shown lawyers suffer mental health problems at higher rates than the general U.S. population, though the new study does not draw such comparisons. While the study methodologies differed slightly, rates of anxiety, stress and depression were each higher than those found in the 2016 report. The rate of hazardous drinking, however, had declined. Consistent with the earlier study, younger lawyers reported mental health challenges at higher rates than their older counterparts, with the study authors theorizing that the stress of being a novice in a demanding profession, a lack of professional support, and educational debt are contributing factors. Mental health and wellness also varied by practice area, the study found. Lawyers working in house at companies or in judicial chambers reported lower levels of distress and burnout than did solo practitioners and those in private practice. Lawyers at law firms reported higher levels of hazardous drinking while attorneys involved in litigation had higher rates of burnout and hazardous drinking — which the study authors said could be the result of the “adversarial exposure” of litigation alongside long hours. Lawyers working the most hours per week are also the most at risk of burnout, the study found. Those working more than 71 hours a week were approximately three times as likely to screen positive for moderate to severe stress as were those working between 31 and 40 hours a week. Concerns over confidentiality and potential harm to their professional reputations remain the top barriers cited by lawyer respondents to seeking help for their mental health and wellness challenges, the study found. DOCS SHOW KING & SPALDING FEE CAP FOR FEDERAL RESERVE WORK Law firm King & Spalding’s contract for legal work for the Federal Reserve involving a U.S. Justice Department investigation into Jerome Powell was capped at $1.5 million, according to newly disclosed legal records obtained by Reuters. The law firm’s contract in January originally set a $750,000 maximum but was later bumped up to $1.5 million, the records showed. Reuters last week obtained the contract from a records request. The Federal Reserve [USN:L1N40115M TEXT:"hired"] King & Spalding for legal guidance as the Justice Department investigated then-Fed Chairman Powell over renovation costs for Fed buildings. Prosecutors in April said they were dropping their inquiry of Powell for now. A federal judge in March [USN:FWN4010NW TEXT:"blocked"] subpoenas targeting Powell, in a rebuke of the Justice Department. Powell has denied any wrongdoing. The King & Spalding team included former Republican-appointed U.S. attorney Robert Hur and two other partners, Andrew Michaelson and Leah Grossi, the records showed. The board redacted the lawyers’ discounted hourly rates. It is common for private attorneys to reduce rates for government clients. The firm and the Federal Reserve did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Powell has [USN:S0N3YT04W TEXT:"chosen to continue serving"] on the Fed board. His term lasts until early 2028. He turned to lawyers from Williams & Connolly for his defense. LEGAL SECTOR JOB GROWTH CONTINUES The U.S. legal sector hit another historic employment high in August as job growth in the broader economy [USN:L1N44W0EC TEXT:"accelerated"], according to figures released last week by the U.S. Department of Labor. The total number of jobs in the legal sector, including lawyers, paralegals, judges and legal assistants, stood at 1,245,900 in August, an increase of 600 from July and up 7.8% compared to five years earlier, figures released by the department's Bureau of Labor Statistics show. The sector has added jobs every month but one over the last two years, BLS data shows. By contrast, the U.S. finance sector, which is larger and an important source of income for law firms, lost 11,000 jobs last month. That sector has shrunk by 125,000 jobs since peaking in May 2025, per BLS. The legal sector job growth comes as large U.S. law firms recorded double-digit revenue gains in the first half of 2026 thanks to an increase in billing rates and strong demand fueled in part by work related to AI, according to survey data [USN:L6N44M0Y5 TEXT:"released last month by Wells Fargo"]. Read more: [USN:L6N44S168 TEXT:"Rival lawyers clash over fees after $2.8 billion Blue Cross settlement"] [USN:L6N44F19B TEXT:"Lawyers square off in fight over voice data used to train AI"] [USN:L6N44411J TEXT:"US Supreme Court case tests fees for immigration detainees"]

item.title: Trump administration charges in some high-profile cases falter
item.description: President Donald Trump's administration has brought a number of high-profile cases, some of which have been dropped, dismissed or blocked by judges or juries.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump 's administration has brought a number of high-profile cases, some of which have been dropped, dismissed or blocked by judges or juries. Here are some of the cases. REFLECTING POOL The Justice Department [USN:S0N3ZQ017 TEXT:"dropped"] its case against former U.S. Olympian David Hearn, who was accused of vandalizing the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, part of Trump's efforts to [USN:L1N3YZ1G0 TEXT:"remake Washington"]. In a July 31 court filing, federal prosecutors said evidence pointed to a flawed installation, not vandalism, as causing the liner of the newly renovated pool to peel. Trump, facing criticism over the $14.7 million renovation, had repeatedly blamed the problems on vandals he alleged had sabotaged the project. Hearn, 67, pleaded not guilty to felony destruction of property. He had acknowledged reaching into the pool to touch a section of already detached liner, but denied ever removing a piece. Lawyers for the former Olympic canoeist accused the Trump administration of using the case to provide "political cover" for mismanagement of the project. SANDWICH THROWER, OTHER ASSAULTS ON FEDERAL OFFICERS Christian Garcia was charged with assaulting a federal officer in June 2025 immigration protests in Santa Ana, California. He admitted to throwing a plastic water bottle toward officers but said the wind blew it back onto him. Garcia, 32 at the time, was arrested and held for three days, then lost both his jobs after his bosses told him they had been called by investigators. Federal prosecutors dropped the case in January with no explanation. The Trump administration has [USN:L6N43V0Z5 TEXT:"brought criminal charges"] against at least 851 people accused of attacking or impeding federal officers, only to abandon them at an unusually high rate. A Reuters review of federal court records completed in July found that 31% of completed cases had ended in dismissal. That compares to 8% of all federal criminal cases, according to Federal Judicial Center data. Separately, former Justice Department staffer Sean Dunn, who hurled a sandwich at a Customs and Border Protection agent in fury over Trump’s law enforcement surge in Washington, was cleared of misdemeanor assault charges in November 2025 after a three-day trial. Prosecutors initially sought felony charges against Dunn, but downgraded the case to a misdemeanor after a grand jury [USN:FWN3UJ0IK TEXT:"declined to return"] an indictment, one of [USN:L6N3UI0MT TEXT:"several cases in which"] grand juries refused to indict. LETITIA JAMES New York Attorney General Letitia James, a longtime Trump critic, was [USN:L6N3U50OF TEXT:"charged"] in October 2025 with lying on a mortgage application. A federal judge [USN:S0N3U5043 TEXT:"dismissed "]the criminal charges the following month, saying the Trump-picked U.S. attorney who brought the case was unlawfully appointed. In December, a federal grand jury in Virginia refused to indict James on allegations of mortgage fraud for the second time, according to sources familiar with the matter. James, an elected Democrat, characterized the case as an abuse of the criminal justice system designed to punish her for her criticism of Trump and a [USN:L1N3UD0JT TEXT:"lawsuit"] she led against Trump and his family real estate business. JAMES COMEY Former FBI Director James Comey, whom Trump fired in 2017 as the bureau investigated possible collusion between his 2016 presidential campaign and Russia, became a harsh critic and frequent target of the president. The Justice Department filed criminal charges against Comey in September 2025 alleging false statements and obstructing a congressional investigation over Comey's 2020 testimony when he [USN:L1N2GR1AY TEXT:"addressed Republican criticism"] of the Russia investigation. In November, a federal judge dismissed charges against Comey, saying the U.S. attorney who brought the case was unlawfully appointed. In April, the Justice Department charged him with threatening Trump by posting a 2025 photo of seashells arranged on a North Carolina beach to show the numbers "86 47." In U.S. parlance, the number 86 can be used as a verb meaning to throw somebody out of a bar, while 47 could be seen as code for Trump, the 47th president. Comey's lawyers said the case was a [USN:L6N3VW0VA TEXT:"vindictive prosecution"].

item.content:encoded:

MADRID, Sept 10 : Kimi Antonelli looks more and more like Formula One's next champion but the Mercedes driver said on Thursday he wanted to push title thoughts to the back of his mind and just focus on driving. The 20-year-old told reporters at the Spanish Grand Prix that winning his home Italian race at Monza in front of tens of thousands of cheering compatriots last Sunday, from 19th place on the grid after engine penalties, had been the best day of his life "so far". Eating spaghetti out of the winner's silver trophy also tasted pretty good, and Antonelli said his WhatsApps had exploded with messages from the likes of MotoGP great Valentino Rossi, but there was still a long way to go and he was not about to be distracted. "I don't really want to drive thinking about championships," he said.

"I think Monza was the proof that I wasn't driving thinking about or worrying about the championship. I was just driving to win, to do my best.    "Of course there might be occasions in the future where, before taking a certain decision, I might think about the championship. But the thing I want to avoid is going on a track for a free practice or a qualifying or even a race thinking about or worrying about the championship. That's the thing I want to avoid at all costs." Antonelli is 66 points clear of teammate George Russell, the pre-season favourite who is running out of races to get back in the game. The Briton has won two races to the Italian's seven, including five in a row. "I think I would definitely need some luck and some good performances," Russell said of his own chances. "It's not really something I'm thinking about because as I said right now he's performing better than me so he deserves to be leading the championship... I'm focused on driving faster and just finding more performance." The new Madring circuit hosts the Spanish Grand Prix for the first time this weekend, with all drivers facing a new challenge.

item.title: Perú se une a coalición antidroga de EEUU tras visita de Rubio; Fujimori anuncia "nueva era"
item.description: Perú se unirá a la coalición de Estados Unidos contra los cárteles de la droga y el crimen trasnacional, anunció el jueves la presidenta Keiko Fujimori, tras la visita del secretario de Estado estadounidense, Marco Rubio, en su última parada de una gira que incluyó Colombia y Ecuador.
item.dc:creator: Marco Aquino, Kylie Madry
item.content:encoded: Perú se unirá a la coalición de Estados Unidos contra los cárteles de la droga y el crimen trasnacional, anunció el jueves la presidenta Keiko Fujimori, tras la visita del secretario de Estado estadounidense, Marco Rubio, en su última parada de una gira que incluyó Colombia y Ecuador. Perú formará parte del "Escudo de las Américas", que reúne ahora a varios países con líderes de derecha o conservadores de América Latina, en lo que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ha calificado como una campaña agresiva para hacer frente a los cárteles de la droga. Perú y Colombia son los dos mayores productores de cocaína en el mundo, según organismos internacionales. "Me alegra informar a nuestro país, que el Perú formará parte del Escudo de las Américas, coalición multilateral en la que participan más de quince países y que es liderada por los Estados Unidos", dijo el mandataria peruana tras la cita. "Empezamos una nueva era de las relaciones entre el Perú y los Estados Unidos", destacó luego en una conferencia de prensa. Fujimori dijo en una conferencia de prensa que la participación de Perú en la coalición permitirá "actuar con más rapidez", el intercambio de inteligencia y reforzar la acción conjunta contra los grupos criminales a través de las fronteras. Rubio, quien celebró la decisión, dijo que la iniciativa busca "proteger a la región" de las organizaciones que amenazan la soberanía de los países del hemisferio. "La amenaza hoy día son grupos transnacionales, porque acuérdense que había una época en que estos grupos operaban dentro de territorios nacionales solamente, pero hoy día es una red de terroristas", agregó. La visita de Rubio, el viaje de más alto nivel de Estados Unidos a Perú desde el regreso del presidente Donald Trump al poder, se da en un momento en que Washington busca estrechar lazos comerciales y de seguridad con gobiernos conservadores de América Latina, a la vez que contrarresta la influencia de China en la minería y la infraestructura. LA SOMBRA DE CHINA China, que tiene grandes minas de cobre y ha incursionado en negocios en energía e infraestructura en Perú, el tercer mayor productor de cobre del mundo, posición que otorga a esta relación un peso estratégico adicional para ambos gobiernos. Ante una pregunta sobre la criticas de Estados Unidos sobre el avance e China en Perú, Fujimori destacó que los tres países forman parte de la alianza Asia-Pacífico, llamada APEC, y que seguirá aprovechando la relación entre sus miembros. "Perú tiene una gran producción de minerales, de productos pesqueros, productos agrarios, y va a seguir en ese esfuerzo de seguir teniendo intercambios comerciales con diferentes países del Asia", dijo Fujimori, que asumió al poder en julio. China opera desde fines del 2024 un megapuerto de aguas profundas en Perú, que ha reducido los tiempos de viaje marítimo a Asia y se ha convertido en un centro de tránsito para mercancías como vehículos eléctricos con destino a los mercados regionales. Según datos oficiales, el intercambio comercial de Perú con China, que este año superaría los 50.000 millones de dólares, es más del doble frente a Estados Unidos. Perú tiene con ambos países un pacto de libre comercio desde hace más de una década. Sin mencionar a China, Rubio dijo en la conferencia que es interés de Estados Unidos mejorar el comercio con Perú. "Más allá de esto, hay una oportunidad extraordinaria comercial; hemos hablado de esto y hay oportunidades reales de trabajar juntos en acuerdos y movimientos comerciales que van a ser extraordinariamente beneficiosos para Perú", indicó. Perú espera de Estados Unidos un alivio de los aranceles estadounidenses, luego de que Trump elevó la tasa a 12,5% a productos procedentes de 60 socios comerciales, incluido Perú, debido a acusaciones a las acusaciones de una aplicación laxa de las prohibiciones sobre el trabajo forzoso. Perú y Estados Unidos, que tiene 200 años de relación, ya han tomado medidas para profundizar sus lazos de defensa. En enero, Estados Unidos designó a Perú como un importante aliado no perteneciente a la OTAN, y el Departamento de Estado aprobó una posible venta militar extranjera de 1.500 millones de dólares para trabajos de diseño y construcción en la base naval del Callao, el principal centro naval peruano cerca de Lima. En Lima, los funcionarios de ambos países discutieron también el apoyo de Estados Unidos a los preparativos de Perú ante una posible emergencia por El Niño, según indicó Fujimori. La parada en Perú culminó la gira de Rubio por tres países de Sudamérica, tras sus visitas a Colombia y Ecuador, centrada en la lucha contra el narcotráfico, la migración y el comercio.

item.title: India's NSE seeks $46 billion valuation in trimmed IPO, launch next week
item.description: National Stock Exchange of India has set a price band of 1,700-1,785 rupees ($17.81-$18.70) per share for its long-awaited IPO, which launches next week and could rank among India's biggest-ever listings.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: National Stock Exchange of India (NSEI.NS) has set a price band of 1,700-1,785 rupees ($17.81-$18.70) per share for its long-awaited IPO, which launches next week and could rank among India's biggest-ever listings. NSE could be valued at up to 4.42 trillion rupees ($46.31 billion) at the top end of the price range, a public filing showed early Friday, making it one of the most valuable companies in the country and within reach of Nasdaq (NDAQ.O) and London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG.L) . India's largest bourse had on Thursday cut the size of its IPO by more than 15% as some top investors trimmed the number of shares they intended to sell, which a [USN:L4N45209D TEXT:"source told"] Reuters was primarily on account of a lower-than-expected price band. The $2.36 billion IPO will likely trail an upcoming offering by billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Jio expected to raise $3.8 billion and Hyundai Motor India's (HYUN.NS) $3.3 billion issue in 2024. The offering comes after years of delays and at a time when India's IPO market is regaining momentum after a sluggish start to the year. NSE's share sale will open for subscription on September 17 and close on September 21, with anchor investor bidding scheduled for September 16. The stock is expected to list on or about September 24. NSE, the country's biggest exchange by trading volumes, dominates the derivatives market and has benefited from a surge in retail trading in the world's most populous country. PRICING LOWER THAN EXPECTED NSE is not selling new shares in the IPO and will not receive proceeds. Existing investors including State Bank of India (SBI.NS) and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board are offloading a total 126.4 million shares, down from the 148.91 million planned earlier. SBI is selling the most shares at about 16 million, while its unit SBI Capital Markets was added to the list of selling shareholders. MS Strategic (Mauritius) - a Morgan Stanley fund, is selling 31% fewer shares at 11 million. The primary reason for the reduced share sales is the lower-than-expected price band, with shareholders believing they will get a better valuation in the secondary market post listing, a source told Reuters on Thursday ahead of the official pricing announcement. In an informal market where unlisted shares of NSE trade, the price has ranged from 2,000 rupees to 2,100 rupees, according to recent deals. Tighter market rules have weighed on the likely pricing of the issue, three sources said. The Securities and Exchange Board of India last year announced tighter curbs on retail participation in the options trading market. Tighter bank funding curbs, higher taxes on derivatives trading and India's newly launched closing auction session have also weighed on trading volumes. In the quarter ended June 30, NSE's net profit rose 6.7% to 31.2 billion rupees, while revenue from operations rose 13% to 45.6 billion rupees. ($1 = 95.4400 Indian rupees)

item.title: An opioid appeal test limits of judicial power in mass torts
item.description: After nearly a decade of litigation and $50 billion in settlements, the nationwide opioid litigation brought by local and state governments finally seemed to be winding down. Then the Ohio federal judge overseeing it allowed hundreds of plaintiffs this summer to add two deep-pocketed defendants to their cases.
item.dc:creator: Jenna Greene
item.content:encoded: After nearly a decade of litigation and $50 billion in settlements, the nationwide opioid litigation brought by local and state governments finally seemed to be winding down. Then the Ohio federal judge overseeing it allowed hundreds of plaintiffs this summer to add two deep-pocketed defendants to their cases. The judge's move has prompted an urgent appeal by the companies, pharmacy benefit managers Optum Rx and Express Scrips, which argue that the judge made a procedural error by allowing the parties to amend their complaints en masse years after the deadline to do so had passed. The companies, which deny wrongdoing, argue that U.S. District Judge Dan Aaron Polster should have evaluated the requests of all 800 plaintiffs — ranging from small rural towns like Cherokee, Alabama, to major American cities including Detroit and Cleveland — individually. The appeal now before the Cincinnati-based 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals highlights a central tension in multidistrict litigation: How much leeway should judges have to deviate from the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure when managing the massive proceedings? If the appeals court finds the judge overstepped, it likely doesn’t mean Optum and Express Scripts would escape the litigation altogether. But it could force plaintiffs to clear additional hurdles before adding the companies to their cases, slowing the litigation and potentially easing settlement pressure on the defendants. The procedural dispute comes after many of the opioid litigation's largest players, including drugmakers, distributors and pharmacy chains, agreed to [USN:L1N3SJ0KO TEXT:"settlements"] over their alleged roles in a crisis that has killed more than 800,000 people since 1999. The pharmacy benefit managers, however, remain in the MDL along with some retail pharmacies and generic drugmakers. The plaintiffs allege that Optum and Express Scripts, which process claims for insurance coverage of prescription medications, colluded with drugmakers to promote opioids, oversupplying communities with addictive medications. A spokesperson for Optum, which is owned by UnitedHealth Group and generated $ 154.7 billion in revenue in 2025, said in a statement that the company “did not contribute to this crisis, and on the contrary has been a leader in fighting opioid abuse.” Express Scripts, which was [USN:KCN1OJ2DM TEXT:"bought by Cigna"] for $54 billion in 2018 and no longer releases stand-alone revenue, declined comment. A spokesperson for the plaintiffs’ legal team, which includes lawyers from Motley Rice; Simmons Hanly Conroy; Farrell & Fuller and Spangenberg, Shibley & Liber, declined to comment. In the early days of the opioid litigation, which began in 2017, pharmacy benefit managers were named as defendants in fewer than 100 lawsuits. Polster in court papers later described the companies' business practices as "unusually opaque," which may have made them a less-obvious initial target. In 2024, plaintiffs’ lawyers asked Polster for permission to amend hundreds of complaints to add Optum and Express Scripts as defendants. In part, they pointed to "key information" produced in litigation brought by Jefferson County, Missouri, that they said shed new light on the role of the companies in the opioid crisis. But their request came five years after Polster’s March 16, 2019, deadline for most litigants to make such changes. This is where the Rules of Federal Civil Procedure come into play. Rule 15 says judges should allow parties to amend their lawsuits “when justice so requires.” And Rule 16 says changes are permitted if plaintiffs can demonstrate a “good cause” for their failure to comply with the original schedule. Defense lawyers from Sullivan & Cromwell; Alston & Bird and Quinn, Emanuel, Urquhart & Sullivan argue that Polster erred by allowing the plaintiffs to add their clients without first conducting a case-by-case analysis. In a court order, the judge said it would require “colossal resources” to look at each case individually, and that doing so would not serve the efficiency goals of an MDL. Instead, he issued a series of rulings addressing common issues, ultimately allowing the 800 amended complaints. Defense lawyers counter that federal rules don’t allow such a shortcut, and that the judge was required to consider if each plaintiff individually satisfied Rule 15 and Rule 16. Many do not, they argue. For example, they say the plaintiffs and their lawyers had access to the relevant documents about pharmacy benefit managers as early as July 2018, but failed to act on the information. They also note that in 2020, the Sixth Circuit reversed Polster for a similar procedural move in the opioid MDL, rebuking him for allowing two Ohio counties to add untimely claims. “MDLs are not some kind of judicial border country, where the rules are few and the law rarely makes an appearance,” the panel held . The MDL court “must find efficiencies within the Civil Rules, rather than in violation of them.” Now defense lawyers want the Sixth Circuit again to determine whether Polster crossed the line, and to reinforce its earlier warning that the rules of civil procedure offer no exception for multidistrict litigation. The procedural question prompted a trio of amicus briefs last week in support of the pharmacy benefit managers. The U.S. Chamber of Commerce in its brief warned of potentially “devastating” effects on American businesses and the national economy if MDL judges aren't required to follow the same procedural rules that govern other civil cases. The Chamber also noted that MDLs now account for nearly two-thirds of all private civil litigation at the federal level, writing that they are “the predominant means for suing businesses in federal court today.” Mandamus petitions – where a litigant asks an appeals court to intervene before a case reaches final judgment – are rarely granted. But the pharmacy benefit managers’ protest appears to have piqued the Sixth Circuit’s interest. The appellate court ordered plaintiffs' lawyers, and "invited" Polster, to respond by Sept. 15.

item.title: Is Trump's $5,000 'dividend' legal and how would it work?
item.description: President Donald Trump on Wednesday proposed a $5,000 Trump dividend payment to U.S. adults if his Republicans retain control of the House of Representatives and the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Andy Sullivan, Jonathan Stempel, Saqib Ahmed
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump on Wednesday proposed a [USN:L1N45203G TEXT:"$5,000 "Trump dividend" payment"] to U.S. adults if his Republicans retain control of the House of Representatives and the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections . Here is what we know about Trump's pledge: WHO WOULD GET THE MONEY AND WHERE WOULD IT COME FROM? Trump said the checks would go to all adult U.S. citizens -- about 240 million people, according to the U.S. Census. That would cost a total of $1.2 trillion. Vice President JD Vance suggested on Fox News after Trump's speech that the U.S. government could draw on tariff revenue, which has been juiced by Trump's trade wars . The Congressional Budget Office estimates the government has taken in $167 billion so far in the fiscal year that ends September 30 -- not nearly enough to cover the cost of Trump's proposed giveaway. The payments would instead widen the government's budget gap, which is already at a level that [USN:S0N43F052 TEXT:"alarms budget watchdogs"]. CBO estimates the government will spend $2.1 trillion more than it collects in revenue in the current fiscal year and projects that figure will grow in the years to come as the population ages. WOULD THE PAYMENTS BE LEGAL? Candidates regularly promise benefits in return for votes. During the 2024 presidential campaign, Trump promised tax breaks for seniors, tipped workers and other targeted groups —and delivered them in his "One Big Beautiful Bill" the following year. Democratic candidates, including President-elect Joe Biden, promised a third round of COVID-19 relief checks in a Georgia special election in 2021 and delivered when they won control of Congress. The U.S. Supreme Court has ruled that a comparable promise is legal. In a unanimous 1982 decision, the high court overturned a lower-court ruling that had invalidated the election of a Kentucky official who had promised to save taxpayer money by lowering county commissioners' salaries. Elon Musk, the world's richest person, [USN:L6N42X16V TEXT:"offered voters a chance to win $1 million"] in 2024 if they signed a petition to support the Constitution. That drew legal challenges, still unresolved, from voters who said they had no real chance to win because Musk was seeking people to support his political action committee, which backed Republican candidates. It would be difficult to challenge Trump's dividend in court, as voters might have trouble showing that they had been directly harmed. WOULD THIS HAVE TO PASS CONGRESS? Yes. Congress has authority over spending under the U.S. Constitution. Trump's Republicans control both the House and the Senate by narrow margins, and several members of his party have already reacted favorably to the idea. Democrats would be sure to oppose any legislation and could block passage in the Senate, where a supermajority of 60 votes is needed to advance most legislation. Republicans could invoke a complex budget process to bypass Democrats and approve the bill along party lines. They have successfully used this approach twice since Trump's January 2025 return to office, but have struggled to advance a third such package. They have little time to act before the November 3 elections, as the House is scheduled to be in session for only one week before then. Congress could also try to act in a "lame-duck" session after the election. HAS THE U.S. GOVERNMENT GIVEN MONEY DIRECTLY TO CITIZENS BEFORE? Yes. Congress approved three separate direct payments in March 2020, December 2020 and March 2021 as part of sweeping relief packages to help people weather the economic disruption from the COVID-19 pandemic. Those payments — up to $1,200, $600 and $1,400 per adult, respectively — were phased out for higher-income people. That amounted to 476 million payments totaling $814 billion, according to a congressional oversight committee. Investigators found numerous logistical problems, including fraud and $1.4 billion sent to dead people. HOW WOULD THIS AFFECT THE ECONOMY AND FINANCIAL MARKETS? Economic studies have shown that the pandemic-era stimulus checks contributed to the subsequent rise in inflation by substantially boosting consumer demand. Those payments also boosted the stock market, with a measurable spike in retail trading volumes following each wave of stimulus deposits. But Trump's proposed dividend could upend bond markets if the government funded it through borrowing. The massive influx of new Treasury debt, combined with revived inflation fears, could drive bond prices sharply lower and send yields soaring. That could push government borrowing costs higher, further pressuring the U.S. budget at a time when interest payments already exceed military spending. Yields on [USN:L4N4520VC TEXT:"benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury bonds"] ticked up to 4.91% on Thursday as investors assessed Trump's proposal. HAS TRUMP MADE SIMILAR PROMISES IN THE PAST? Trump promised a similar $2,000 dividend in November 2025 tied to tariff revenue and said it would not apply to wealthy people, though no follow-up action was taken. Trump successfully sent a one-time "warrior dividend" payment of $1,776 to roughly 1.45 million military members in December 2025, drawing on money already approved by Congress. On Thursday, Trump's White House said nearly 1 million Americans will get [USN:FWN4520NI TEXT:"$500 payments"] to account for what it describes as excess fees charged for Affordable Care Act health insurance.

item.title: 【欧州市況】短期債売られる、ECBの利上げ観測が拡大－株は3日続落
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 10日の欧州債券市場は、短期債が下落した。欧州中央銀行（ECB）が利上げを決定し、インフレ見通しを引き上げたことを受け、追加利上げ観測が拡大した。英国でも、イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）による追加利上げが織り込まれ、国債は大幅下落した。

ドイツ2年国債利回りは一時13ベーシスポイント（bp、1bp＝0.01%）上昇して3.20%と、2023年10月以来の水準を付けた。10年債利回りは6bp高い3.51%と、2009年以来の高水準となった。

短期金融市場は現在、ECBが来年6月までに25bpの利上げをさらに3回行うと、完全に織り込んでいる。

英国債も売られた。2年債利回りは17bp上昇して4.87%と、約3年ぶりの高水準に達した。

欧州株は3日続落した。原油価格の急騰やECBの新たな経済予測を受け、インフレへの懸念が強まった。

ストックス欧州600指数は0.7%下落し、7月以来の安値で取引を終えた。銅価格の下落を背景に鉱業株が最も大きく下げた。一方、北海ブレント原油が1バレル＝105ドルを突破したことを受け、エネルギー株は相対的に堅調だった。フランスのCAC40指数は0.5%下落し、年初からの上昇分を失った。

原題：Europe Bonds Drop as ECB Rate Hike Bets Jump: End-of-Day Curves、European Stocks Decline on Inflation Worries After ECB, US Data（抜粋）

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for financial services industry
item.description: OpenAI on Thursday launched a version of ChatGPT built for the financial services industry, combining its latest AI model with built-in data from providers including LSEG , PitchBook and Daloopa to target investment bankers and equity researchers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: OpenAI on Thursday launched a version of ChatGPT built for the financial services industry, combining its latest AI model with built-in data from providers including LSEG (LSEG.L) , PitchBook and Daloopa to target investment bankers and equity researchers. The product, ChatGPT for Financial Services, was developed with Morgan Stanley (MS.N) and Evercore (EVR.N) as design partners to help shape the offering, OpenAI said in a blog post. The launch reflects a broader push by AI companies to build products for regulated industries where data governance and security are central concerns. The product builds on ChatGPT Enterprise's existing security controls, including role-based access and encryption, and allows compliance teams to export workspace logs into audit workflows. The service is powered by GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI's newest model, which the company said was built to improve retrieval across financial data tools, financial reasoning and the accuracy of generated content. Users can conduct research across multiple sources, build financial models and generate client materials such as pitchbooks using their firm's own templates, OpenAI said. OpenAI said it plans to expand the breadth of financial data available through the product and further train its models to identify, interpret and apply that information across tasks traditionally handled by experienced analysts. The product includes datasets from Daloopa, LSEG News, PitchBook, Crunchbase, Quartr and others covering earnings transcripts, financial statements and company fundamentals. OpenAI said the data is indexed on its own infrastructure to improve retrieval and citation. LSEG serves as the sole distributor of Reuters news, financial data, and real-time alerts to global financial professionals. Firms that already hold data subscriptions can connect them through integrations with FactSet (FDS.N) , S&P Global, Preqin and Datasite, the company said. OpenAI said it plans to expand the product beyond investment banking and equity research across the wider financial services sector.

Sept 10 : England's Lottie Woad will make her eagerly awaited Solheim Cup debut alongside Charley Hull against unbeaten American duo Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz in Friday's foursomes at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands. Europe are seeking to reclaim the team trophy after the U.S. won in Virginia in 2024. The 22-year-old Woad faces a tough start against world number one Korda, who has won all four of her foursomes matches alongside Corpuz in the last two editions. But Woad, one of four rookies in Anna Nordqvist's team, will be able to count on the experience of Hull, who is making her eighth successive appearance.

Friday's other foursomes will see Europe's Nanna Koerstz Madsen and Celine Boutier take on Alison Lee and Lauren Coughlin, Esther Henseleit and Leona Maguire against Andrea Lee and Lindy Duncan and Maja Stark and Linn Grant playing Rose Zhang and Jennifer Kupcho. "Charley and Lottie, they've got to play (together) quite a bit on tour this year, so I think they were both very excited to be paired with each other," Nordqvist said after the draw. "If you are going to be anywhere (on Friday) you want to be on the first tee because it doesn't get better than that." U.S. captain Angela Stanford said pairing Korda and Corpuz was her easiest selection decision. "If I didn't put those two out (Korda and Corpuz), I would be questioned. I feel like the whole world knew that they were coming," she said on Thursday. "We can talk about Nelly and we can talk about her being the number one player in the world, but don't sleep on Allisen. I've called her the backbone of our team." The U.S. are trying to retain the trophy and claim a first victory on European soil since 2015. The last three editions in Europe have all been titanic tussles with no more than one point separating the sides who are tied on 42 points apiece from those matches. Three years ago in Andalusia the U.S. team led 4-0 after Friday foursomes, but Europe hit back to clinch a thrilling 14-14 tie after Sunday's singles to retain the trophy. "Even if you're a couple down early, you can get it back and even just getting a half point could be vital," Woad said as she looked ahead to her debut. "So I think you've just got to have that mentality that any half point or point helps."

Source: Reuters

item.title: Peru to join US anti-drug coalition 'Shield of the Americas' after Rubio visit
item.description: Peru will join the U.S.-led "Shield of the Americas" coalition against drug cartels, President Keiko Fujimori said on Thursday during U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit, deepening cooperation and tightening security ties with Washington early in her presidency.
item.dc:creator: Marco Aquino
item.content:encoded: Peru will join the U.S.-led "Shield of the Americas" coalition against drug cartels, President [USN:L6N43Q0ZQ TEXT:"Keiko Fujimori"] said on Thursday during U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit, deepening cooperation and tightening security ties with Washington early in her presidency. Speaking at a joint news conference, Fujimori said Peru's participation in the coalition would speed intelligence-sharing and bolster joint action against criminal groups operating across borders. Rubio welcomed Lima's decision, saying the initiative was meant to "shield the region" from organizations that threaten the sovereignty of countries across the hemisphere. He reiterated that the region was a priority for Washington. "U.S. getting involved in the region is not a favor. It is essential to our own security, to our own prosperity, to our own well-being in America. And this administration is committed to this," he said, adding there would be more similar initiatives. The top U.S. diplomat's trip to Peru, the last stop of a three-country swing to Latin America that also included Ecuador and Colombia, is the highest-level U.S. visit to the country since President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025. The visit, which focused on counternarcotics, migration and trade, comes as Washington seeks closer security and commercial ties with conservative governments in Latin America while pushing back against China's influence in mining and infrastructure. Peru is the world's third-largest copper producer. The two countries have already moved to deepen defense ties. In January, the United States designated Peru a major non-NATO ally, and the State Department approved a possible $1.5 billion foreign military sale for design and construction work at Callao Naval Base, Peru's main naval hub. "We appreciate this opportunity (to join the initiative), because for us, having previously had to tackle terrorism, (we) know how difficult it is to confront criminality today," Fujimori said. She was apparently referring to the period of political violence driven by the Maoist Shining Path insurgency that her father, former President Alberto Fujimori, cracked down on during his decade in power from 1990 to 2000. Peru's [USN:S0N42A02L TEXT:"Foreign Ministry"] had flagged in recent months that Lima might join the Shield of the Americas as part of a broader push to strengthen border security and coordination against transnational crime. Officials also discussed U.S. support for Peru's preparations for a possible emergency related to the El Niño weather phenomenon, Fujimori said. Rubio's trip coincided with the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, where Trump hopes to energize core supporters and help the party hold onto its congressional majorities. 'NOT ANYONE'S BACKYARD' Peruvian government sources said the country was also seeking relief from U.S. tariffs after Trump raised duties in late July to 12.5% from 10% on imports from 60 trading partners, including Peru, citing failures to stop imports involving forced labor. While Peru has traded largely tariff-free under a 2009 agreement, the new duties have hit Peru's agricultural exports, specifically blueberries, grapes and avocados. As Lima negotiates the removal of those duties, China continues to outpace the United States in trade with Peru. Peru's trade with China rose 35% in the first half of the year, surpassing a 20% increase in trade with the U.S., according to official data. The figures put bilateral trade with China on track to surpass the more than $50 billion recorded in 2025, compared with roughly $19 billion in trade with the United States that year. China's embassy in Peru defended its trade and political ties this week ahead of Rubio's visit. Beijing operates copper mines and has expanded its footprint in Peru's energy and infrastructure sectors. "The Western Hemisphere is not anyone's 'backyard'," the Chinese embassy in Lima said late on Tuesday on X.

item.title: In-house counsel group accuses rival of training AI on its materials
item.description: The Association of Corporate Counsel, a nonprofit bar association for in-house attorneys, sued competitor The L Suite in Delaware federal court on Thursday for allegedly copying its materials to train a lawyer-focused chatbot.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: The Association of Corporate Counsel, a nonprofit bar association for in-house attorneys, sued competitor The L Suite in Delaware federal court on Thursday for allegedly copying its materials to train a lawyer-focused chatbot. The lawsuit said that The L Suite trained its chatbot Lloyd on copyrighted works including at least one ACC report, and that it "brazenly" promoted Lloyd with an image of the report and an ACC trademark. Spokespeople for The L Suite did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the complaint. "We made a good-faith effort to resolve this matter directly, and when that effort failed, filing this complaint became necessary to protect our members’ interests and the integrity of ACC’s work," ACC president Jason Brown said in a statement. The Washington-based ACC has more than 48,000 members and publishes content, including continuing legal education materials, surveys and white papers. The L Suite, which calls itself "the leading general counsel community on its website," announced the launch of its Lloyd chatbot in May. The L Suite said in a press release that Lloyd "combines foundational AI capabilities with the trusted judgment of thousands of accomplished in-house legal executives." The ACC said in its complaint that an L Suite video promoting Lloyd displayed the cover of an ACC report. "As a result, there can be no doubt that The L Suite was specifically aware that its Lloyd platform was utilizing ACC materials," the lawsuit said. The ACC also alleged that The L Suite violated its trademark rights in the phrase "By In-House Counsel, For In-House Counsel" by using "Built By In-House Counsel, For In-House Counsel" in its Lloyd advertising. The ACC requested monetary damages and a court order blocking The L Suite from using its trademarks and copyrighted materials. The case is Association of Corporate Counsel v. The L Suite Inc, U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, No. 1:26-cv-01138. For the ACC: Robert Leighton and Paul Sauerteig of Goldberg Kohn For The L Suite: attorney information not yet available

Madring gives F1 a blind date with 'Monumental' mayhem

FAST

MADRID, Sept 10 : Formula One rolls into Madrid this weekend for a first look at the Madring, a new Spanish Grand Prix venue with a banked beast of a corner and enough unknowns to have drivers reaching for the word of the day: challenging. Spain is hosting two races this season, with Madrid's street circuit around the IFEMA exhibition centre following Barcelona's Catalunya Grand Prix on the calendar. The Madring is the first new circuit since Las Vegas three years ago and brings down the curtain on the regular European leg of the season. The Madring's signature flourish comes at Turn 12, where "La Monumental" slings the cars around a long, banked arc before spitting them over a crest, leaving drivers momentarily aiming at grandstands built to hold up to 45,000 fans — and the blue sky — rather than tarmac.  Until now, most of the field have only met the circuit in the simulator, leaving teams to untangle set-ups and racing lines on a layout whose pecking order remains guesswork.

"It looks different. It looks that the track has character, that is charismatic, with a lot of different kinds of corners," Madrid-born Williams driver Carlos Sainz, an ambassador for the track, told a press conference on Thursday. "At least we can take that away, that that is going to be a different track to what we're used to." Sainz has driven a few laps in a road car on an unfinished version of the track, but said that was "nowhere as representative as the laps that I did in the simulator". Ferrari pair Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton are the only other drivers with some prior experience of the Madring after driving there during a filming day in July, when the circuit was still more building site than Grand Prix theatre. Hamilton, the seven-times world champion, was quick to pour cold water on any suggestion of an advantage. "I think it's hardly any," he told reporters. "It was dusty, super, super dusty. There was zero grip. We couldn't change the car because it's not a test. It was filming. "We weren't even flat out in many of the corners. We were low, just low power, low grip. The benefit, the only one thing is I've seen which way the track goes. So honestly, I don't think we have any advantage." SWEEPING SPECTACLE The circuit is built partly inside Madrid's convention centre and partly on the streets of Valdebebas, across from soccer side Real Madrid's training ground. Its mix of enclosed sections, tight walls and sweeping spectacle has intrigued drivers, though overtaking may be at a premium. La Monumental, with its diagonal banking and vast grandstand backdrop, carries echoes of American oval racing and has the potential to feel more like a stadium than a conventional circuit. Hamilton said the layout reminded him partly of Montreal's kerbs, but compared the difficulty of learning it to Saudi Arabia's Jeddah circuit, introduced in 2021. "It's a massively challenging circuit," he said. "Of all the new tracks that I've gone to, this one, maybe Saudi, I like the two closest in terms of how difficult it was to get on top of the car and find the right lines." Leclerc also expects qualifying to take on extra weight. "It looked like a very challenging track, and I think exactly the kind of track that I enjoy as a driver," he told reporters. "It's true to say as well that I think coming Sunday the amount of overtaking opportunities there will be will be very little, but I think in qualifying it will be a very cool and challenging track for all drivers." That could make Saturday the weekend's main act. "I think it's the kind of weekend where you want to focus more on the qualifying pace than on the race pace," Leclerc said. "The priority will be shifted a little bit more towards qualifying."

Source: Reuters

item.title: 中国問題の緊急性増す欧州、強硬策を協議－報復回避もなお模索
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： ドイツ人技術者のゼンケ・ジークフリートセン氏は、浮体式洋上風力発電タービンの画期的な設計をあみ出し、4月にはスペインのサンチェス首相にその設計を提案した。しかし、このエピソードにはもどかしさも残る。

この設計の考案に、ジークフリートセン氏は7年を費やした。ところが、この設計を基にした革新的な2基のローターを備えた浮体式プラットフォームをサンチェス氏に紹介したのは、同氏から1基当たりのライセンス契約で特許を買い取った中国の再生可能エネルギー機器メーカー、明陽智慧能源集団だった。

何よりつらかったのは、ジークフリートセン氏自身の会社が欧州で提携先を見つけられず、3カ月前に事業を停止していたことだ。

ジークフリートセン氏はインタビューで、「中国の実業家は、私の設計の助けを借りて事業を成功させることができた」と述べた。

この件は欧州企業が中国の競合に、競争力や戦略、資金力でますます後れを取っていることを示す数多くの事例の一つに過ぎない。

欧州でこうした不満が出るのは今に始まったことではない。太陽光発電でも、そうだった。中国は欧州から設備を輸入してノウハウを蓄積・習得し、大規模な生産で欧州の競合企業を圧倒した。

だが、この問題は欧州連合（EU）各国の首脳にとって、緊急性を増している。10月にブリュッセルで開かれる首脳会議では、新たな関税措置や輸出規制、投資審査を組み合わせで中国への対応を打ち出すことを目指している。

ブルームバーグ・エコノミクス（BE）の新たな分析によると、ここ数年で中国メーカーに市場シェアを奪われたことによるEU27カ国の経済的な影響は、2025年に域内総生産（GDP）の0.7%、金額にして約1500億ドル（約23兆1000億円）に達した。前年の推計ではGDP比0.5%だった。

BEの貿易担当エコノミストで、マエバ・クザン氏とともにリポートを執筆したニコール・ゴートンカラテッリ氏は、「先端製造業で中国は急速にシェアを拡大している」と指摘した。

FAST

BUDAPEST, Sept 10 : Had the World Athletics Ultimate Championship existed in his prime, Usain Bolt says he would have been first in line to compete, drawn not only by the chance to race the world's best but also by the richest prize pot in the sport's history. "I was having a conversation with Asafa (former world record-holder Powell). We were actually talking about that same thing," Bolt said on Thursday. "We're like, 'jeez, we missed out with this cash prize.'" Winners of individual events pocket $150,000, while the winning relay teams share $80,000, meaning a sprinter contesting the 100, 200 and mixed 4x100 metres relay could leave Budapest with a tidy sum. "I won a few championships, and it still doesn't add up to all the cash, so it's big," said Bolt, the 100m and 200m world record-holder. "It's good for the sport, it incentivises athletes to do their best. Sorry I missed out on it."
